In syllable-timed languages every syllable takes roughly equal time; English is stress-timed, so only the stressed syllables are evenly spaced and everything else speeds up or slows down to fit.
This is why English can sound 'fast' in the unstressed parts and 'slow' on stressed words.

English is stress-timed: you stress the words that carry meaning and squeeze the rest.
Strong: nouns, main verbs, adjectives, adverbs, question words.
Weak: articles, prepositions, auxiliaries, pronouns.
